neighbours.label: circadian / body-clock context: text about daily biological rhythms, sleep-wake timing, melatonin and light-dark entrainment (fires on function tokens inside such text)
fire: Bright light in the evening delays the circadian clock and makes it harder to fall asleep.
Travellers crossing many time zones find their sleep-wake cycle out of step with the local day.
The pineal gland secretes melatonin at night, signalling to the body that it is time to rest.
Night-shift nurses struggle because their body clock still expects darkness and sleep.
Mice kept in constant dim light drift to a daily rhythm slightly longer than 24 hours.
The suprachiasmatic nucleus acts as the master clock that keeps the body's daily rhythms in time.
Chronobiology studies how organisms keep time with the cycle of day and night.
Teenagers' internal clocks shift later, so early school start times cut into their sleep.
quiet: Bright colours in the kitchen make the room feel larger and more cheerful.
Travellers crossing many borders find their paperwork checked at every station.
The thyroid gland secretes hormones that regulate how fast the body burns energy.
Night-shift nurses struggle because the ward is short of staff and supplies.
Mice kept on a high-fat diet gain weight slightly faster than the control group.
The cerebellum acts as the coordinator that keeps the body's movements smooth.
Seismology studies how waves travel through the layers of the Earth.
Teenagers' growth spurts come later for boys, so heights even out by sixteen.

notes: Probing: melatonin/pineal 0.73, 24-hour cycle in darkness 0.48, circadian rhythm 0.44, internal clock 0.36, jet lag 0.35; heart, insulin and a drummer's rhythm at 0.10 or less. Output promotes entr-, phot-, mel-, pine-, zeit-.
